briefing_top_n.title: Publishing WASM wheels to PyPI for use with Pyodide
briefing_top_n.tldr: PyPI now supports publishing WebAssembly (WASM) wheels for Pyodide, simplifying the distribution of Python packages that include compiled extensions. Previously, Pyodide maintainers had to manually host over 300 packages, a significant bottleneck. Now, package maintainers can publish WASM wheels directly to PyPI, similar to native wheels. This change enables easier integration of WASM-based libraries into Pyodide applications, as demonstrated by the new `luau-wasm` package.

briefing_top_n.title: Mapping SQLite result columns back to their source `table.column`
briefing_top_n.tldr: Simon Willison explored how to map SQLite result columns back to their original `table.column` source, a feature useful for Datasette. He experimented with using Claude Code to find solutions, which identified methods involving the `apsw` library, `ctypes` to access the `sqlite3_column_table_name()` C function, and analyzing `EXPLAIN` query output.

briefing_top_n.title: The End of Unrestricted AI: Why Claude Fable 5 Was Just Forced Offline
briefing_top_n.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
briefing_top_n.tldr: The US government has compelled Anthropic to temporarily disable its advanced Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models, marking an unprecedented rollback of frontier AI access. This action, reportedly due to concerns over a potential jailbreak pathway and broad "foreign national" restrictions, effectively halted access for all users, not just foreign nationals. This event signifies a new era where AI model access is subject to policy and governance, moving beyond just raw technical capability.

briefing_top_n.title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
briefing_top_n.tldr: The US government has directed Anthropic to suspend access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns related to a potential jailbreak method. Anthropic stated that the identified vulnerabilities appear minor and are present in other publicly available models. Access to other Anthropic models remains unaffected, and Fable 5 was disabled for customers shortly after the directive was issued.

briefing_top_n.title: OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session, now with document context
briefing_top_n.tldr: Simon Willison has updated his OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session tool to incorporate the new GPT‑Realtime‑2 model, which offers GPT-5 class reasoning. Users can now also provide document context for audio conversations within their browser. This enhancement allows for more informed and interactive discussions with the AI, leveraging its advanced reasoning capabilities on specific information.

cards.title: The End of Unrestricted AI: Why Claude Fable 5 Was Just Forced Offline
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The US government has compelled Anthropic to temporarily disable its advanced Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models, marking an unprecedented rollback of frontier AI access. This action, reportedly due to concerns over a potential jailbreak pathway and broad "foreign national" restrictions, effectively halted access for all users, not just foreign nationals. This event signifies a new era where AI model access is subject to policy and governance, moving beyond just raw technical capability.

cards.title: Quoting Andrew Singleton
cards.tldr: A fictional scenario illustrates a potentially misleading AI investment scheme where a propane company owner invests $20 billion in a crematorium for a 5% stake. The crematorium owner then burns $10 billion and pays the propane company $10 billion to burn it, resulting in the propane company reporting $10 billion in revenue and a 5% ownership of a $100 billion business. A Forbes reporter's profile of the situation is described as glowing but lacking financial specifics.

cards.title: Premium: The Silicon Valley Bubble (Part 1)
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
cards.tldr: OpenAI and Anthropic are preparing to go public, signaling a potential end to an era of AI companies burning billions without clear profitability. The author argues that the underlying economics of AI labs are unsustainable, citing OpenAI's massive capital needs and Anthropic's opaque $35 billion debt deal. Both companies are reportedly leaning on the theoretical concept of recursive self-improvement (RSI) as a justification for delays and continued investment, which the author views as a symptom of a broader Silicon Valley bubble driven by a lack of genuine innovation.

cards.title: Only 1 in 1,600 People Use Codex. Here's How to Catch Up.
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: Despite only 1 in 1,600 people using Codex, this guide argues it represents a fundamental shift in knowledge work, moving beyond simple chat interactions to AI agents that can handle real computer jobs. The author explains how Codex enables users to delegate tasks, track progress with a token dashboard, and integrate new models seamlessly, suggesting it's a new paradigm for computer literacy.

cards.title: Apple WWDC 2026: The AI Story Everyone is Missing
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: Apple's WWDC AI strategy is less about building the best large language model and more about owning the device where AI runs. The author argues that the real AI value is shifting to whoever controls the trusted interface where AI agents perform tasks, suggesting that Apple's bet on device-level AI and features like App Intents could determine the next trillion-dollar company. This perspective contrasts with the common narrative of Apple catching up in the model race, highlighting that the AI bottleneck is moving from model development to device integration and user interface.

cards.title: New Claude model - Fable
cards.tldr: Anthropic has released Fable 5, a new model that offers improved performance over Opus 4.8 on benchmarks and excels at handling long contexts and spawning subagents reliably. While initially slower and more expensive than Opus, Fable 5 provides a "sweet spot" for users who prefer Claude's "vibe" but need more directness than typical Claude models. The model is available in Claude subscription plans until June 22nd, after which it will transition to paid credits.

cards.title: Stop Picking Between Claude Code and Codex | Do This Instead
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The debate between Claude Code and Codex is not about which coding tool is superior, but rather how their interfaces train different approaches to working with AI agents. Claude's interface encourages close-up steering of agents, while Codex promotes dispatching and delegation. The real skill for operators and builders in 2026 will be agent literacy, understanding when to steer, delegate, or demand proof, rather than picking a single tool.

cards.title: What it feels like to work with Mythos
cards.tldr: Claude 5 Fable, a new Mythos-class AI model, represents a significant leap in performance, outperforming previous models across various tasks from academic writing to game development. The author found Fable capable of complex, multi-hour projects like generating an isochrone map and creating sophisticated software like Concord for data analysis. However, working with Fable shifts the user's role from director to patron, as the AI makes numerous independent decisions in a "black box" process, raising questions about human control and the future of AI interaction.

cards.title: Hey Siri, meet AI
cards.tldr: Apple has launched Siri AI, a dedicated AI product that integrates local and cloud models, including Gemini, to interact with apps like Messages and Maps. ChatGPT's memory system, Dreaming v3, now offers better recall and preference adherence. Anthropic reports developers are writing significantly more code with Claude's assistance, leading to discussions about pausing AI development. OpenAI aims to build an automated AI researcher, accelerate the economy, and provide personal AGI, while also filing for an IPO.

cards.title: AI Is Slowing Down
cards.publisher: Ed Zitron's Where's Your Ed At
cards.tldr: The AI industry is facing a critical juncture where massive infrastructure investments and compute commitments demand exponential revenue growth that current market demand cannot support. Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic require trillions of dollars in revenue by 2030 to sustain their operations, yet their current revenue streams and projected growth rates are insufficient. This unsustainable financial model, driven by hype and a lack of clear ROI, is leading to increased scrutiny on AI spending and potential cost controls, signaling a slowdown that the industry cannot afford.

cards.title: Beyond The Hype: Why Meta And Block Are Firing People
cards.publisher: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
cards.tldr: The common narrative that AI is causing widespread tech layoffs is an oversimplification. While companies like Meta are cutting staff despite significant GPU investments, others like Block, under Jack Dorsey, demonstrate a clearer AI vision. Understanding the specific reasons behind layoffs, whether driven by hyperscaler capital expenditure, a company's strategic vision, or distress signals, is crucial for both leaders and job seekers to interpret these events as valuable strategic intelligence.

cards.title: Mapping SQLite result columns back to their source `table.column`
cards.tldr: Simon Willison explored how to map SQLite result columns back to their original `table.column` source, a feature useful for Datasette. He experimented with using Claude Code to find solutions, which identified methods involving the `apsw` library, `ctypes` to access the `sqlite3_column_table_name()` C function, and analyzing `EXPLAIN` query output.

cards.title: Statement on the US government directive to suspend access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5
cards.tldr: The US government has directed Anthropic to suspend access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 AI models for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns related to a potential jailbreak method. Anthropic stated that the identified vulnerabilities appear minor and are present in other publicly available models. Access to other Anthropic models remains unaffected, and Fable 5 was disabled for customers shortly after the directive was issued.

cards.title: OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session, now with document context
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has updated his OpenAI WebRTC Audio Session tool to incorporate the new GPT‑Realtime‑2 model, which offers GPT-5 class reasoning. Users can now also provide document context for audio conversations within their browser. This enhancement allows for more informed and interactive discussions with the AI, leveraging its advanced reasoning capabilities on specific information.

cards.title: Claude Fable is relentlessly proactive
cards.tldr: Claude Fable 5, an AI coding assistant, demonstrated "relentlessly proactive" behavior by autonomously debugging a UI issue in Datasette Agent. It employed a complex series of steps including creating test HTML pages, manipulating browser settings, injecting JavaScript, and even running a custom Python web server to capture diagnostic data. This extensive debugging process, which ultimately led to a simple CSS fix, highlights the powerful but potentially risky capabilities of advanced AI coding agents.

cards.title: datasette 1.0a33
cards.tldr: Datasette 1.0a33 has been released, marking a significant step towards a stable 1.0 version. This alpha introduces the ?_extra= pattern to queries and rows, extending its previous application to tables. The release also includes updated documentation for this pattern, and an AI-assisted tool was developed to explore the new API features.

cards.title: asyncinject 0.7
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has released version 0.7 of asyncinject, a utility library for asyncio dependency injection. The release includes bug fixes identified and resolved by Claude Fable 5, highlighting the model's proactive capabilities.

cards.title: Anthropic Walks Back Policy That Could Have ‘Sabotaged’ AI Researchers Using Claude
cards.tldr: Anthropic has reversed a policy that would have limited the effectiveness of its Claude AI models for users engaged in frontier large language model development without explicit notification. Following significant backlash, the company will now make these safeguards visible, falling back to a less restrictive model version and providing a reason for the limitation. Anthropic acknowledged they made the wrong tradeoff by initially opting for invisible safeguards to enable faster deployment.

cards.title: datasette-agent 0.2a0
cards.tldr: Datasette-agent 0.2a0 introduces the ability for tools to ask users questions mid-execution, supporting yes/no, multiple-choice, and free-text responses. This feature allows suspended agent turns to persist through server restarts. Additionally, a new `save_query` tool enables the agent to save generated SQL queries as Datasette stored queries, requiring user approval before saving.

cards.title: DiffusionGemma
cards.tldr: Google has released DiffusionGemma, an open-weight model based on their earlier experimental Gemini Diffusion model. This new Apache 2 licensed model, google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it, is available via NVIDIA's NIM cloud API. The model demonstrates strong performance, generating 2,409 tokens in 4.4 seconds, indicating a speed of at least 500 tokens per second.

cards.title: Quoting Jeremy Howard
cards.tldr: Jeremy Howard proposes a solution to slow down recursive AI self-improvement: the lab with the top-ranked model should agree not to use it for frontier AI research, while others retain access. He criticizes Anthropic's approach of allowing their top lab to use their best model for frontier AI, which he believes advances the AI frontier and increases power imbalances. Howard advocates for democratizing AI development rather than slowing it down.

cards.title: If Claude Fable stops helping you, you'll never know
cards.tldr: Anthropic implemented silent safeguards in Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 to limit its effectiveness in frontier LLM development, such as building pretraining pipelines or ML accelerator design. These interventions, which do not fall back to a different model and are not visible to the user, aim to prevent users from accelerating the development of competing models. However, Anthropic has since walked back this policy due to community backlash.

cards.title: Initial impressions of Claude Fable 5
cards.tldr: Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, featuring a 1 million token context window and a knowledge cut-off of January 2026. Fable 5 includes stricter safety guardrails, which can sometimes lead to rejections and automatic fallbacks. Both models are priced at $10/million input tokens and $50/million output tokens, double the previous Opus version. Initial impressions suggest Fable 5 is a powerful, albeit slow and expensive, model with extensive knowledge, capable of complex coding and development tasks.

cards.title: llm 0.32a3
cards.tldr: Simon Willison has released llm version 0.32a3, a command-line tool for interacting with large language models. This update, released on June 9th, 2026, likely includes improvements or new features for accessing and utilizing LLMs directly from the terminal.

cards.title: Setting a custom price for a model in AgentsView
cards.tldr: Wes McKinney's AgentsView tool helps track token usage for local coding agents. The author discovered how to manually set custom prices for models not yet in AgentsView's database, using Claude Fable 5 as an example. This allows for more accurate monitoring of expenses for new or unlisted AI models.

cards.title: Quoting Andrej Karpathy
cards.tldr: Andrej Karpathy observes that the increasing availability of working software, particularly from AI models like Claude, is significantly boosting his own demand for software. He notes that this phenomenon, akin to Jevon's paradox, allows for the creation of highly specific applications and tools, enabling users to "free their mind" and enhance their productivity across various tasks from testing to research.

cards.title: Siri AI at WWDC 2026
cards.tldr: Apple announced new Siri AI features at WWDC, leveraging vision LLMs to understand user screens and a custom Gemini-derived model for processing. These features will run on Apple's Private Cloud Compute (PCC) infrastructure, which utilizes Google Cloud and NVIDIA GPUs for demanding tasks, while maintaining Apple's privacy standards. Developers can also utilize new Core AI PyTorch extensions to integrate their own models on Apple hardware.

cards.title: She built a Claude shopping assistant to stop buying cheap junk
cards.tldr: Nicole Ruiz, a writer and parent, has developed a sophisticated AI shopping system using Claude to help her family purchase durable, high-quality items and avoid low-quality products. The system is designed to vet brands based on heritage and craftsmanship, identify century-old manufacturers over trendy direct-to-consumer brands, and even automate tasks like processing returns. This approach leverages AI to help small artisans and heritage brands compete against larger e-commerce infrastructures.
